explanations: The provider slot Put has no ConditionExpression. The patient-side item always has a fresh sk (it includes the new appointmentId), so its attribute_not_exists check never fails. Two patients booking the same provider slot concurrently (or one after another) both succeed: the second Put silently overwrites the provider's SLOT item, while both patients keep an appointment record. The slot Put needs ConditionExpression: "attribute_not_exists(pk)".

providerDay queries the provider pk with begins_with(sk, 'SLOT#date'), and patientUpcoming queries the patient pk with sk >= APPT#from. Duplicating items per access pattern is standard NoSQL modeling. It isn't a backup, DynamoDB has no two-key requirement, and single-item transactions are allowed.

BookingService normalizes slotStart with toISOString, so sort keys look like SLOT#2026-03-02T09:15:00.000Z and a prefix match on the date picks up exactly that day. No scan, day item, or GSI is involved.

recordAudit runs after the transaction, outside the try/catch, so its error propagates to the caller while the appointment is already committed. It isn't in the transaction, isn't a SlotConflictError, and isn't swallowed.
